Alex —

Thanks for the questionnaire. Below are concise answers for the hosted API (if you want a one-page summary I attached our Hosted Data Lifecycle document and a per-account retention matrix).

1) Region pinning
- Hosted API: customers can request data to be served and stored in a specific public cloud region (we currently support US (us-east-1), EU (eu-west-1), and APAC (ap-southeast-1) for hosted accounts).
- Region pinning is selectable at provisioning and enforced at the account level. For strict legal/regulatory requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments (BYOK/KMS options available).

2) Primary data retention (customer content)
- Active (primary) store: customer-submitted content is retained for the life of the resource by default; customers may configure TTL per-tenant.
- Default retention policy for standard hosted accounts: 90 days for conversational context + metadata, unless a longer retention is explicitly configured.
- For immediate erasure requests we remove data from the primary store within 24 hours of request processing (see erasure process below).

3) Backup & snapshot retention
- Automated snapshots/backups are region-scoped (not replicated outside the selected region) by default.
- Snapshot retention: up to 30 days for standard hosted accounts. Snapshots are encrypted and included in erasure workflows (see below).
- Geo-replication of backups is an opt-in enterprise feature (Dedicated/Private or add-on).

4) Cache & KV/KV-cache (in-memory)
- Short-lived caches/kv caches: typically purged within 72 hours; any persisted cache artifacts are cleared as part of erasure workflows.

5) Logs and telemetry
- Operational logs (request traces): retained 180 days for debugging and incident response.
- Security/audit logs (access logs, auth events): retained 365 days by default for compliance/forensics.
- Access to raw logs can be provided via a support request (see export SLA).

6) Erasure / deletion process
- Customer requests (console/API) trigger a multi-step erasure: a) remove references and metadata from primary stores (target: <24h), b) purge caches (target: <72h), c) mark backups for deletion and remove cryptographic keys where applicable (depends on snapshot retention windows; full removal from backup indexes targeted within 30 days), d) final verification and audit log entry.
- For hosted accounts we provide attestation that erasure completed; Dedicated/Private can get shorter windows via contractual SLAs.

7) Encryption & key management
- All customer data in-hosted is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3).
- For hosted API we manage KMS keys by default. BYOK / customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private deployments only; discuss if you require BYOK for hosted — we can raise as an enterprise exception.

8) Export & audit support
- We can produce per-account export packages (data inventory and logs) upon request. Standard support SLA for exports is 10 business days; expedited delivery can be added by contract.

9) Compliance & attestations
- Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II and publishes a summary of controls. We also provide supporting artifacts under NDA for due diligence.

Attached: redwood-hosted-data-lifecycle-overview.pdf; retention-matrix-axion.csv

If you want, I can join a 30-minute call to walk through this and map to your control set.

—Mateo

- Are automated snapshots ever geo-replicated (for DR) by default, or only if we opt into the enterprise add-on? Our compliance team is asking whether backups may cross a region boundary without explicit consent.
- For the export package you mentioned, does the export include backups/snapshots or only primary-store content and logs?

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API: data locality + retention questionnaire

Alex —

Following up on Mateo's answers with the precise policy language you can cite in your review: 

• Snapshot replication: by default, automated snapshots for hosted accounts are region-scoped and are not geo-replicated without the customer's explicit opt-in. Geo-replication is available as a paid add-on or as part of a Dedicated/Private deployment offering.

• What snapshots contain: snapshots capture encrypted application data and metadata required for restore. Backups are treated as customer data and are subject to the same erasure and retention controls; they are included in export packages when the export request explicitly includes backups (this is an opt-in parameter in the export request).

• Export SLA: standard export includes primary-store content, metadata, and requested logs. To include snapshots/backups in the export, please indicate this when filing the request; the export SLA remains 10 business days by default.

For your convenience I've uploaded an excerpt you can paste into your questionnaire: 

"Redwood Inference stores hosted-account data in the region selected at account provisioning. Automated snapshots are region-scoped by default and are not geo-replicated without explicit customer opt-in. Snapshot retention windows for standard hosted accounts are 30 days; backups included in export or erasure workflows are removed according to the account's configured retention and deletion schedule. Encryption at rest is AES-256; encryption keys for hosted accounts are managed by Redwood unless BYOK is contracted for Dedicated/Private deployments."

Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-data-lifecycle

—Irene
